record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: In cuprate superconductors, are electronic inhomogeneities intrinsic and generic across the family or only a pathology of some compounds, and to what extent does the stripe picture survive in materials such as Bi2212 where STM reveals apparently random patchy inhomogeneity?

evidence.quote: Currently, this is a much debated area of research in high critical temperature superconductors, and it is unclear whether cuprates are intrinsically inhomogeneous in all its forms, or whether the inhomogeneities are a pathology of only a fraction of the Cu oxides. It is also unclear to what extend the notion of stripes, with at least partial order in its dynamical form, survives the Bi2212 evidence of inhomogeneities where the patches are totally random.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of hole-doped cuprate high-temperature superconductors (e.g., La$_{2-x}$Sr$_x$CuO$_4$, YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6+x}$, Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+\delta}$ (Bi2212), and related layered copper-oxide compounds). Experiments such as neutron and X-ray scattering reveal, in some compounds, charge and spin "stripe" correlations — quasi-one-dimensional modulations of charge and spin density on the CuO$_2$ planes with at least partial (often dynamical) order. In other compounds, notably Bi2212, scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) of the local superconducting gap and local density of states reveals a patchy, apparently random spatial inhomogeneity on the nanometer scale, without obvious stripe-like one-dimensional order.

Address the following questions rigorously:

(a) Are nanoscale electronic inhomogeneities an intrinsic, generic feature of the entire cuprate family in the underdoped-to-optimally-doped regime, or are they a non-universal property (a "pathology") found only in a subset of the compounds? Specify a precise sense in which "intrinsic" and "generic" can be defined (for example, robustness against improving sample quality, presence in chemically distinct families, and independence of disorder strength), and determine whether such a property holds.

(b) To what extent does the stripe picture — i.e., a description in terms of (possibly fluctuating) unidirectional charge/spin density modulations — remain an appropriate effective description in compounds such as Bi2212, where STM observations indicate a seemingly random patchy inhomogeneity rather than ordered stripes? Determine whether the Bi2212 STM observations are compatible with disordered/short-range or dynamic stripe correlations, or whether they require a genuinely different organizing principle (e.g., checkerboard order, pair density wave, or quenched-disorder-driven electronic glass).
artifact.status_search_result: The questions of whether nanoscale electronic inhomogeneity in cuprates is intrinsic/universal and whether the stripe picture extends to Bi2212 remain actively debated in the condensed-matter literature. Multiple post-2010 reviews and experimental studies continue to report intrinsic gap inhomogeneity in Bi2212 and identify stripe/charge-order fingerprints in several cuprate families, but no consensus solution has been established.

status_evidence.title: Structural aspects of materials with static stripe order
status_evidence.snippet: Fingerprints of stripe correlations have been identified in several hole doped cuprate families including Bi2212.
status_evidence.claim: Stripe correlations are reported across multiple cuprate families, but their relation to Bi2212 STM patchiness remains debated.

status_evidence.title: STM/STS study of electronic states in highly underdoped Bi2212
status_evidence.snippet: Intrinsic spatial electronic inhomogeneity on nanometer length scale, manifested in spatial inhomogeneity of the superconducting gap.
status_evidence.claim: Bi2212 continues to exhibit intrinsic nanoscale gap inhomogeneity as seen in STM, without consensus on its origin.

status_evidence.title: Incoherent strange metal sharply bounded by a critical doping in Bi2212
status_evidence.snippet: Recent Bi2212 studies continue to probe the phase diagram and nature of electronic states.
status_evidence.claim: The microscopic nature of inhomogeneity and order in Bi2212 remains an active research area.
